L131: # Pricing
L132: 
L133: Last updated Aug 7, 2026|Copy as Markdown|cite87†View as Markdown |cite78†Agent setup L134:

L137: R2 charges based on the total volume of data stored, along with two classes of operations on that data:
L138: 
L139:   1. cite88†Class A operations which are more expensive and tend to mutate state.
L140:   2. cite89†Class B operations which tend to read existing state.
L141: 
L142: For the Infrequent Access storage class, cite90†data retrieval fees apply. There are no charges for egress bandwidth for any storage class.
L143: All included usage is on a monthly basis.
L144: 
L145: Note
L146: 
L147: To learn about potential cost savings from using R2, refer to the cite91†R2 pricing calculator ↗︎†r2-calculator.cloudflare.com .
L148: ## R2 pricing
L149: 
L150:  | Standard storage  | Infrequent Access storage
L151: --- | --- | ---
L152: Storage  | $0.015 / GB-month  | $0.01 / GB-month
L153: Class A Operations  | $4.50 / million requests  | $9.00 / million requests
L154: Class B Operations  | $0.36 / million requests  | $0.90 / million requests
L155: Data Retrieval (processing)  | None  | $0.01 / GB
L156: Egress (data transfer to Internet)  | Free ^{cite92†1 }  | Free ^{cite92†1 }
L157: 
L158: Billable unit rounding
L159: 
L160: Cloudflare rounds up your usage to the next billing unit.
L161: 
L162: For example:
L163:   * If you have performed one million and one operations, you will be billed for two million operations.
L164:   * If you have used 1.1 GB-month, you will be billed for 2 GB-month.
L165:   * If you have retrieved data (for infrequent access storage) for 1.1 GB, you will be billed for 2 GB.
L166: ### Free tier
L167: 
L168: You can use the following amount of storage and operations each month for free.
L169: 
L170:  | Free
L171: --- | ---
L172: Storage  | 10 GB-month / month
L173: Class A Operations  | 1 million requests / month
L174: Class B Operations  | 10 million requests / month
L175: Egress (data transfer to Internet)  | Free ^{cite92†1 }
L176: 
L177: Caution
L178: 
L179: The free tier only applies to Standard storage, and does not apply to Infrequent Access storage.
L180: ### Storage usage
L181: 
L182: Storage is billed using gigabyte-month (GB-month) as the billing metric. A GB-month is calculated by averaging the peak storage per day over a billing period (30 days).
L183: 
L184: For example:
L185: 
L186:   * Storing 1 GB constantly for 30 days will be charged as 1 GB-month.
L187:   * Storing 3 GB constantly for 30 days will be charged as 3 GB-month.
L188:   * Storing 1 GB for 5 days, then 3 GB for the remaining 25 days will be charged as `1 GB * 5/30 month + 3 GB * 25/30 month = 2.66 GB-month`
L189: For objects stored in Infrequent Access storage, you will be charged for the object for the minimum storage duration even if the object was deleted or moved before the duration specified.
L190: ### Class A operations
L191: 
L192: Class A Operations include `ListBuckets`, `PutBucket`, `ListObjects`, `PutObject`, `CopyObject`, `CompleteMultipartUpload`, `CreateMultipartUpload`, `LifecycleStorageTierTransition`, `ListMultipartUploads`, `UploadPart`, `UploadPartCopy`, `ListParts`, `PutBucketEncryption`, `PutBucketCors` and `PutBucketLifecycleConfiguration`.
L193: ### Class B operations
L194: 
L195: Class B Operations include `HeadBucket`, `HeadObject`, `GetObject`, `UsageSummary`, `GetBucketEncryption`, `GetBucketLocation`, `GetBucketCors` and `GetBucketLifecycleConfiguration`.
L196: 
L197: ### Free operations
L198: 
L199: Free operations include `DeleteObject`, `DeleteBucket` and `AbortMultipartUpload`.
L200: 
L201: ### Data retrieval
L202: 
L203: Data retrieval fees apply when you access or retrieve data from the Infrequent Access storage class. This includes any time objects are read or copied.
L204: ### Minimum storage duration
L205: 
L206: For objects stored in Infrequent Access storage, you will be charged for the object for the minimum storage duration even if the object was deleted, moved, or replaced before the specified duration.
L207: 
L208: Storage class  | Minimum storage duration
L209: --- | ---
L210: Standard storage  | None
L211: Infrequent Access storage  | 30 days
L212: ## R2 Data Catalog pricing
L213: 
L214: R2 Data Catalog charges for catalog operations and compaction data processed, in addition to standard R2 storage and operations. For full details, refer to cite93†R2 Data Catalog pricing .
L215: 
L216: ## Data migration pricing
L217: ### Super Slurper
L218: 
L219: Super Slurper is free to use. You are only charged for the Class A operations that Super Slurper makes to your R2 bucket. Objects with sizes < 100MiB are uploaded to R2 in a single Class A operation. Larger objects use multipart uploads to increase transfer success rates and will perform multiple Class A operations. Note that your source bucket might incur additional charges as Super Slurper copies objects over to R2.

L56: # PostgreSQL Pricing
L57: 
L58: Last verified 30 Sep 2026
L59: 
L60: PostgreSQL is an open source, object-relational database built for extensibility, data integrity, and speed. Its concurrency support makes it fully ACID-compliant, and it supports dynamic loading and catalog-driven operations to let users customize its data types, functions, and more.
L61: 
L62: cite41†Copy page as Markdown cite42†View page as Markdown L63: 
L64: There are two kinds of database cluster plans you can choose from: single node clusters and high availability clusters.
L65:   * Single node clusters begin at $15.00 per month for a single node cluster with 1 GiB of RAM. Single node clusters are not highly available, but they feature automatic failover. We recommend these clusters for preliminary development and testing.
L66: 
L67:   * High availability clusters begin at $30.00 per month for a 2 GiB RAM/1 vCPU primary node with at least one $30.00 per month matching standby node for automatic failover.
L68: You can add or remove standby nodes at any time. Other features, like point-in-time recovery and read-only nodes, vary by database engine. See cite43†Managed Databases feature availability .
L69: 
L70:   * Read-only nodes begin at $15.00 per month. Read-only nodes are replicas of a cluster’s primary node located in additional geographical regions.
L71: 
L72: Additional storage you add to a Standard Edition cluster costs $0.215 per GiB per month.
L73: Advanced Edition clusters begin at $130.00 per month for an 8 GiB RAM/2 vCPU primary node. Standby nodes for high availability and read-only nodes bill at the same rate as the primary node. Additional storage costs $0.115 per GiB per month.
L74: 
L75: Beginning 15 October 2026 for new accounts and 30 November 2026 for all accounts, new Standard Edition clusters cannot use plans with more than 4 GiB of RAM or add standby or read-only nodes. See cite44†PostgreSQL and MySQL plan changes .
L76: Traffic to and from cite6†managed databases does not count against your bandwidth billing transfer allowance.
L77: ## Plans for Cluster Nodes
L78: 
L79: All managed databases are deployed onto Droplets with either cite45†shared or dedicated CPU . For a list of the Droplet plans we offer for PostgreSQL, see the cite46†Managed Databases pricing page†www.digitalocean.com .

L115: ## Frequently asked questions
L116: ###
L117: 
L118: Do you offer any discounts for annual subscriptions?
L119: 
L120: No, we only provide monthly plans.
L121: 
L122: ###
L123: 
L124: Do you offer non-profit or education pricing?
L125: 
L126: No, all plans are currently priced the same for every customer.
L127: 
L128: ###
L129: 
L130: What payment methods do you accept?
L131: 
L132: We accept all major credit cards.
L133: 
L134: ###
L135: 
L136: Is there a free trial available?
L137: 
L138: No, but we provide a free-forever plan.
L139: 
L140: ###
L141: 
L142: Who can I contact about a custom plan?
L143: 
L144: Please contact us at resend.com/enterprise.
L145: ###
L146: 
L147: What happens if I send more emails than my plan allows?
L148: 
L149: With pay-as-you-go pricing, you can continue sending beyond your monthly quota and only pay for what you use. Overages are billed in buckets of 1,000 emails at your plan's overage rate. You can enable this in your team settings under "Transactional Overages." If you don't enable pay-as-you-go and exceed your plan limits, you will be notified and given the option to upgrade to a higher plan.
L150: ###
L151: 
L152: What is the difference between transactional and marketing emails?
L153: In Resend, transactional emails are emails sent using the /emails API, while marketing emails are sent using the /broadcasts API or through the Broadcasts interface in the dashboard. Transactional emails are typically triggered by user actions and include things like password resets or order confirmations. Marketing emails are typically sent to a list of contacts and include things like newsletters or promotional campaigns.
L154: Broadcast emails can only be sent to existing contacts, while transactional emails can be sent to any email address.
L155: ###
L156: 
L157: What does "unlimited broadcast sending" mean?
L158: 
L159: For marketing plans, the focus is on maintaining a relationship with your contacts. Therefore marketing plans are not limited by the number of emails you can send, but only by the number of contacts you have. Broadcasts can only be sent to existing contacts.
L160: ###
L161: 
L162: Do broadcast emails count against the transactional email limits?
L163: 
L164: No. Broadcast emails sent through the /broadcasts API or through the Broadcasts interface in the dashboard do not count against your transactional email limits. Only emails sent through the /emails API count towards your transactional email limits.
L165: ###
L166: 
L167: How are inbound emails counted?
L168: 
L169: Each received email counts towards your transactional emails quota.
